guide.title: Griswold, Connecticut: Jewett City and the Slater Mills
guide.intro: Griswold's roots reach to 1716, when Preston residents tired of traveling south to church organized their own "North Society." The town, then still part of Preston, was incorporated separately in 1815 and named for Roger Griswold, who died in office as governor in October 1812 — a posthumous honor. In the late 1700s Eliezer Jewett opened mills and an irrigation plant at the settlement that came to bear his name; Rhode Islanders John and Lafayette Tibbits founded the Jewett City Cotton Manufacturing Company there in 1809, and in 1823 Samuel Slater, who had helped establish the nation's first cotton mill in Pawtucket, bought the struggling operation with his brother John and renamed it the Slater Company. Jewett City incorporated as a borough of Griswold in 1895. Long before the mills, the Pachaug River was Mohegan fishing ground; stone weirs the tribe built are still visible in Hopeville Pond at low water.

sections.heading: Slater Library and a borough within a town
sections.body: The Slater name is stamped on the borough beyond the mills: the Slater Library at 26 Main Street was a gift of industrialist-philanthropist John Fox Slater, built in 1884 to a Romanesque Revival design by Stephen C. Earle, with the Fanning Annex added in 1930. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in January 2002. Griswold covers 37.1 square miles at the northeastern edge of New London County, with a 2020 census population of 11,402, and contains the borough of Jewett City plus the villages of Doaneville, Glasgo, Hopeville, Kaalmanville, Nathanieltown, Pachaug and Rixtown. John Cantius Garand, designer of the M1 Garand rifle, is among its notable residents.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Griswold sits in Connecticut's Quiet Corner along I-395: take Exit 21 for Route 12 into Jewett City, Exit 22 for Routes 138/164 toward the Pachaug side, or Exit 24 for Route 201 toward Hopeville. There is no passenger rail station anywhere in Griswold or the Borough of Jewett City; rail travelers should ride Shore Line East or Amtrak to New London and finish the trip by car via I-395.

sections.heading: A mill pond, sunflowers and Main Street diners
sections.body: Hopeville Pond State Park sits on a former woolen-mill site with a swimming beach, boating and a wooded campground. Buttonwood Farm, family-owned since 1975, hand-crafts ice cream on site and plants a summer sunflower field for its Sunflowers for Wishes fundraiser, which has raised over $1.9 million for Make-A-Wish Connecticut across two dozen seasons — though the bloom window is a short midsummer stretch separate from the March-through-October ice cream season. Downtown, Charlene's Diner has run a breakfast counter for decades, Mandarin Garden Restaurant serves Main Street Chinese and Asian food, and Uncle Kranky's Cafe and Brewett City Pub anchor the borough's bar-and-grill scene into the evening.

faq.question: How do I get to Griswold?
faq.answer: By car — I-395 Exit 21 (Route 12) reaches Jewett City, Exit 22 (Routes 138/164) serves the Pachaug side, and Exit 24 (Route 201) serves Hopeville. There is no passenger rail station in Griswold; the nearest is New London, reached via I-395.

faq.question: Is there a train to Griswold or Jewett City?
faq.answer: No. No Amtrak, Metro-North, CTrail Hartford Line or Shore Line East station exists in Griswold. The nearest rail is New London Union Station.

faq.question: What is the Slater Library?
faq.answer: An 1884 Romanesque Revival library at 26 Main Street, Jewett City, a gift of industrialist John Fox Slater, with the Fanning Annex added in 1930. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2002; open Monday-Saturday with hours varying by day.

faq.question: Can I still see the sunflowers at Buttonwood Farm?
faq.answer: The Sunflowers for Wishes fundraiser runs a short midsummer window each year; the farm's ice cream stand stays open March 1 through October 31 regardless. Check buttonwoodfarmicecream.com for current-season sunflower dates.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Griswold?
faq.answer: Comfort Inn Griswold, on Voluntown Road near I-395 Exit 22, is the one branded hotel physically inside town. Call ahead to confirm rates and availability.

places.name: Hopeville Pond State Park
places.summary: A former woolen-mill site where Mohegan-built stone fishing weirs are visible in the pond at low water. Swimming, boating, fishing, hiking and a wooded campground of 80 sites plus one rustic cabin. Open daily 8 a.m. to sunset, April to October; recreation field open year-round. Park office (860) 376-2920.

places.name: Pachaug Pond Boat Launch
places.summary: A CT DEEP boat launch at the north end of 841-acre Pachaug Pond, with a concrete-slab ramp and 40 parking spaces. No water-skiing within 1,000 feet of the dam. An active advisory warns that the invasive plant hydrilla has been found in this waterbody — clean, drain and dry your boat.

places.name: Slater Library
places.address: 26 Main Street, Jewett City, Griswold, CT 06351
places.summary: A granite-and-brownstone Romanesque Revival library built in 1884 as a gift from industrialist John Fox Slater, designed by architect Stephen C. Earle, with the Fanning Annex added in 1930. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in January 2002. Open Mon-Wed 12-5:30, Thu 12-6:30, Fri 11-5, Sat 10-2, closed Sunday. Phone (860) 376-0024.

places.name: Buttonwood Farm
places.summary: A working family farm since 1975, hand-crafting ice cream on site with over 50 flavors, open daily noon-8:30 p.m., March 1 through October 31. Each summer the farm plants 14 acres of sunflowers for its Sunflowers for Wishes fundraiser, which has raised over $1.9 million for Make-A-Wish Connecticut; the sunflower field itself is open only for a short midsummer window. Phone (860) 376-4081.

places.name: Mandarin Garden Restaurant
places.address: 31 Main Street, Jewett City, Griswold, CT 06351
places.summary: A long-running Main Street Chinese and Asian kitchen with pickup and delivery. Open Mon, Wed-Thu 11 a.m.-9 p.m., Fri-Sat 11 a.m.-10 p.m., Sun noon-9 p.m., closed Tuesday. Phone (860) 376-1531.

places.name: Brewett City Pub
places.address: 1 East Main Street, Jewett City, Griswold, CT 06351
places.summary: A small independent gastropub — draft beer, cocktails and a food menu — open since late 2023. Despite the name it is a pub, not a working brewery. Evening hours roughly Wed-Sat from 5 p.m., closed Sunday-Tuesday; phone (860) 912-8551.

places.name: Charlene's Diner
places.address: 37 Main Street, Jewett City, Griswold, CT 06351
places.summary: A family-owned downtown breakfast counter opening at 5 a.m. daily, known for its patty melt, blueberry crepes and home fries. Hours Mon 5-11, Tue-Fri 5-1:30, Sat-Sun 5-12:30. Phone (860) 376-9465.

places.name: Uncle Kranky's Cafe
places.address: 37 Main Street, Jewett City, Griswold, CT 06351
places.summary: A midday-to-late-night bar and grill known for its Irish nachos, closed Tuesdays. Hours roughly Mon 4-10 p.m., Wed 12-11 p.m., Thu-Sat 12 p.m.-midnight, Sun 12-10 p.m. Phone (860) 376-4226.

places.name: Comfort Inn Griswold
places.summary: The one branded hotel physically inside Griswold, sited on Route 138 near the I-395 Exit 22 corridor within an easy drive of Foxwoods and Mohegan Sun. Phone (860) 376-3200 to confirm rates and availability.
